summary: Waren Spacefarer, a young pilot, wants forty thousand credits to buy Marta Okafor's Kestrel. He exposed Dren Vasko's people smuggling, but his informant claim won't pay out for months. After a medicine run for Juno Reyes, he took the Halcyon salvage job, which pays forty-five thousand for the recorder and nav core, minus Juno's ten percent. At the tumbling wreck he lost a grapple arm and bruised his ribs. That tore the hatch open, and he went out in his suit and pulled the flight recorder free. The nav core is still thirty metres away at the break, and his last grapple is failing. Now he has to choose between the whole payout and getting out safe.

recent.action: Ask about the deep belt salvage run
recent.narration:
"Tell me about the salvage run."

Juno exhales. "There's an ore freighter called the Halcyon. She broke up three months ago in a rock field out in the deep belt. Her insurer will pay forty-five thousand to whoever brings back her flight recorder and nav core. They want to know whether it was the crew or the ship."

"Why don't you take it?"

"Because the wreck is still tumbling, and the field around it is full of her own debris. I sent a pilot out there in the spring. He came home, but his skiff didn't." Her voice stays even. "I'll lend you a salvage skiff. The insurer pays you and I take ten percent. You'd leave once the strut's fixed."

After her cut, that's the Kestrel.

recent.action: Take the Halcyon job, no hesitation
recent.narration:
"I'll take it." Juno doesn't argue. "Then get some sleep, Spacefarer."

You sleep on a cot in the ridge hab. By morning the crawler has come and gone, and the new strut holds when you lift off. At Bay Nine, Juno hands you the codes to a battered salvage skiff with grapples and a cutting arm. "Bring the skiff back. The money's nice too."

Two days out, the deep belt is dark and quiet. Then the Halcyon slides into your forward view. She's broken in half and tumbling slowly, with glittering debris all around her. The recorder bay is on the aft section, and every eleven seconds it swings past you.
recent.picture: View from a small salvage skiff cockpit with grapple arms visible: a huge ore freighter broken in half, slowly tumbling among glittering debris and dark asteroids in the deep asteroid belt, distant faint sunlight. A lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, at the controls, seen from behind.

recent.action: Scan the wreck before moving closer
recent.narration:
You hold the skiff at a safe distance and let the scanner sweep the wreck. The aft section's spin is steady, which is the only good news. The recorder bay hatch is buckled shut, so you'll need the cutting arm. A twisted hull plate the size of a hangar door is caught in the same tumble, and it sweeps across the bay a few seconds after the hatch passes.

The nav core is closer to the break, where torn cables drift loose.

That gives you about four seconds between the hatch and the plate. It's enough to grapple on, as long as you don't hesitate.

recent.action: Match the spin and grapple the hatch
recent.narration:
You feed in thrust a little at a time until the skiff rolls with the wreck. The stars wheel around you and the Halcyon seems to hold still. The hatch rises into view. You count one, then two, and fire.

Both grapples bite. The skiff shudders and locks to the hull. A heartbeat later the loose plate sweeps past overhead. Its shadow fills the canopy, and it clears your dorsal antenna by about an arm's length.

You're on. You're spinning with her now, so the plate will come back every eleven seconds and pass just as close. The cutting arm unfolds against the buckled hatch. It glows hot and ready, but a full cut will take longer than one gap.
recent.picture: A small battered salvage skiff clamped by grapple arms to the hull of a broken, tumbling ore freighter in the deep asteroid belt. A huge twisted hull plate sweeps just over the skiff's canopy, and a cutting arm glows orange against a buckled hatch. Inside the cockpit is a lean young man in his early twenties with short dark brown hair, light stubble and keen grey eyes, wearing a worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt. Glittering debris, harsh distant sunlight.

recent.action: Grapple the plate and pin it
recent.narration:
You release the port grapple, wait for the plate's shadow, and fire. The claw bites, but it bites at a bad angle. The plate keeps moving and the cable snaps tight.

The skiff is wrenched sideways. Your harness slams into your ribs, metal shrieks, and the port grapple arm tears off at its mount. The cable whips away into the dark, and the plate goes with it, spinning free into the debris field.

You're hanging on by one claw. Alarms are blinking, and your chest burns every time you breathe. But the yank peeled the buckled hatch half open. You can see the recorder's orange casing inside, close enough to reach in a suit.

The plate is gone for now. The wreck is still turning, though, and your last grapple is groaning.
recent.picture: A small battered salvage skiff wrenched sideways against a tumbling broken ore freighter in the deep asteroid belt, one grapple arm torn away with its cable whipping off, a huge twisted hull plate spinning away into glittering debris. Inside the cockpit is a lean young man in his early twenties with short dark brown hair, light stubble and keen grey eyes, wearing a worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, braced against his harness. Red warning lights, harsh distant sunlight.

recent.action: Suit up and grab the recorder
recent.narration:
Your ribs flare as you twist into the suit. Helmet seals, the airlock cycles, and you pull yourself hand over hand along the skiff's hull, while the stars wheel past and the wreck holds still.

The torn hatch edge is razor-sharp. You wedge one boot against it and reach inside. The recorder's clamps are frozen, so you hammer the release with your fist. On the third hit it gives, and the orange casing comes free in your glove.

You clip it to your harness. Then your last grapple groans through the hull and into your bones.

Thirty metres forward, at the break, the nav core blinks faintly among the loose cables. The insurer wants both pieces. Your one claw might not hold long enough for you to get it.
recent.picture: A lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, in a spacesuit with a clear helmet, clinging to a torn hatch on a broken tumbling ore freighter, an orange flight recorder clipped to his harness. A battered salvage skiff is held by one straining grapple nearby, and glittering debris drifts in harsh distant sunlight in the deep asteroid belt.
